settings.name: OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES
settings.description: The proxies whose forwarding headers are believed, as CIDR ranges or single addresses, space- or comma-separated (10.0.0.0/8, 2001:db8::/32, 192.0.2.7); unset, no forwarding header is believed from anyone. From a listed proxy the client address is the right-most forwarding hop that is not listed, and the scheme and host are what that proxy says: the challenge endpoints' and the attester issuance endpoint's per-caller limits, the operator APIs' failed-authentication limit and the attester configuration's advertised URLs use them

when_wrong.detail: An entry that is not an IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR range, or a list of nothing: both challenge endpoints and the attester's issuance and configuration servlets are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and answer 503; the operator APIs ignore every forwarding header and log the reason at ERROR. A /0 range believes every sender and is logged at WARN

settings.name: OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES_HEADERS
settings.description: Which forwarding headers a listed proxy writes: x-forwarded (X-Forwarded-For, -Proto, -Host and -Port) or forwarded (RFC 7239 Forwarded); only that family is read, since a proxy that writes one passes the other through from the client

when_wrong.detail: Not x-forwarded or forwarded, in any case: as OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES. The wrong family leaves the client's own header in place, so the client address and advertised URLs are the client's to choose
